item.text:
Completed a bounded continuation pass across all eight selected chapters without scoring.

New defensible evidence was recovered for:

- 1B: later Zaporizhzhia monitoring, AI safety standards, radiation-safety law, and Belarus nuclear-control uncertainty.
- 2B: October UN findings on torture and detention, Groza civilian deaths, POW/humanitarian access, and Black Sea Initiative termination.
- 3B: UN detention and torture evidence, including occupied-area patterns.
- 4B: electronic voting, limited competition, Khakassia exceptions, and observer-access concerns.
- 5B: 2023 poverty reduction, Social Fund execution reporting, federal budget-execution and audit leads.
- 6B: Social Fund consolidation and 2023 health-ministry reporting.
- 7B: Putin’s published financial disclosure, while preserving the distinction between declared assets and unproven beneficial ownership.
- 8B: government, audit, economic, and implementation evidence; strategic effectiveness remains mixed and attribution-limited.

The strongest newly recoverable units include:

- `WEB-1B-R2-20260805-A01` — IAEA follow-up confirms continuing ZNPP risks and monitoring from 15 November 2023 onward; methodology `["1B.3","1B.8","1B.10"]`. [IAEA report](https://www.iaea.org/sites/default/files/documents/gov2024-9.pdf)
- `WEB-3B-R2-20260805-A01` — UN Commission documented continued Russian torture patterns in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia, including detention-facility abuse; methodology `["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.10"]`. [UN report summary](https://ukraine.un.org/en/250021-un-commission-inquiry-ukraine-finds-continued-war-crimes-and-human-rights-violations-gravely)
- `WEB-4B-R2-20260805-A01` — Swedish Institute analysis found United Russia dominance, limited opposition, nearly four million electronic votes, and weak independent auditability; methodology `["4B.1","4B.3","4B.4","4B.9","4B.10"]`. [Election analysis](https://www.ui.se/globalassets/ui.se-eng/publications/sceeus/russias-september-2023-elections-a-dress-rehearsal-for-vladimir-putin.pdf)
- `WEB-5B-R2-20260805-A01` — Rosstat reported 2023 poverty at 9.3%, down from 2022, while retaining the limitation that this is an aggregate official measure; methodology `["5B.1","5B.8","5B.9","5B.10"]`. [Rosstat poverty data](https://www.rosstat.gov.ru/folder/313/document/232165)
- `WEB-6B-R2-20260805-A01` — Social Fund reported unified administration, synchronized payments, expanded insured coverage, and reviewed 2023 benefit execution; methodology `["6B.1","6B.2","6B.4","6B.9"]`. [Social Fund report](https://sfr.gov.ru/press_center/news/~2024/03/28/262123)
- `WEB-6B-R2-20260805-A02` — Russia’s Health Ministry published a 2023 performance review, but the accessible page mainly confirms the reporting event rather than outcome detail; disposition `context`, methodology `["6B.2","6B.4","6B.5"]`. [Ministry report](https://minzdrav.gov.ru/en/news/2024/04/20/21284-minzdrav-rossii-podvyol-itogi-raboty-za-2023-god)
- `WEB-7B-R2-20260805-A01` — Central Election Commission disclosure reported Putin’s six-year income and its stated sources; this supports formal disclosure only, not absence of concealed assets; methodology `["7B.3","7B.4","7B.6","7B.7"]`. [Disclosure report](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2024/01/30/russian-election-authority-releases-putins-financial-disclosure-a83909/pdf)

Blocked or incomplete targets remain explicitly unresolved: the full IAEA 2023 report endpoint, detailed Social Fund PDF extraction, Rosstat regional microdata, military procurement records, Putin-linked beneficial-ownership evidence, and primary command records.
